title: Smooth trait models, bounded points and volume orders
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $E$ and trait $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. All schemes and morphisms are as in [def-pc-scheme], and products and fibres use [def-pc-base-change]. For a morphism $f:X\to S$, put $\Omega_f^d=\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{X/S}$ using [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. The canonical pullback relation between global $d$-forms along a map $q:Y\to X$ in a base-change square is specified locally: express the source as a finite sum $\sum_i a_i db_{i1}\wedge\cdots\wedge db_{id}$ and the target as $\sum_i q^*a_i d(q^*b_{i1})\wedge\cdots\wedge d(q^*b_{id})$ on neighbourhoods of every point of $Y$. The same relation applies when the target differentials are relative to a further base; in degree zero use the empty wedge.

An open $U$ of an $S$-scheme is base-dense when its inverse image in every scheme-theoretic fibre is dense. A smooth model of an $E$-scheme $X$ is a scheme $M\to T$ that is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and has closed diagonal [def-weil-closed-immersion], with a specified $E$-isomorphism $M_E\simeq X$. It is admissible when its special fibre is nonempty and irreducible. Two models are equivalent if there is an isomorphism over $T$ between base-dense opens, compatible with the identity of $X$ under the specified generic identifications; the opens may be taken to contain their entire generic fibres.

Write $H=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the geometric strict henselization [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with canonical structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], and $F=\operatorname{Frac}H$. All $F$-points of a finite-type $E$-scheme $X$ are bounded when there are a finite affine cover $U_i$, finite algebra generating lists $b_{ij}$ of $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_X)$ over $E$, and integers $c_i$ such that every $F$-point factors through some $U_i$ and satisfies $\pi^{-c_i}b_{ij}(x)\in H$ for every $j$. The inverse image of $H$ includes zero, so this is the valuation convention $v(0)=+\infty$.

For a smooth group scheme $G/E$ [def-sc-group-scheme] of relative dimension $d$, a nowhere vanishing top form means a global section generating $\Omega^d$ at every point, in the sense of [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. Left invariance means that multiplication and the second projection $G\times_E G\to G$ pull the form back to the same form relative to the first factor. For an admissible model $M$ and a nonzero such generic form $\omega$, the order relation $\operatorname{HasOrder}(M,n)$ means that $\pi^{-n}\omega$ extends to a global section of $\Omega^d_{M/R}$ generating it at the generic point of the special fibre. Equivalently this is the stalk definition of order, because on a smooth model with irreducible special fibre the normalized form extends across the codimension-at-least-two complement. The minimum predicate means that some admissible model has the indicated order and every order of every admissible model is at least that integer. A representative list is a finite nonempty list of admissible models with that order such that every admissible model of that order is equivalent to a member; repetitions are allowed.

A permitted shrinking is an open immersion of models over $T$ containing the entire generic fibre and dense in the special fibre, with the same generic identification; its closed complement is therefore contained in the special fibre and nowhere dense there. For a local trait $A$ over $R$, a component open of $M_A$ is the open submodel containing the entire generic fibre and exactly one irreducible component of its special fibre, with the generic identification induced from that of $M$. Component representatives means that every such component admits its open submodel, every component open is admissible of the indicated order, and every minimal $A$-model is equivalent to one of these opens. The smooth base-change predicate for a list and an integer $n_0$ asserts: for every smooth finite-type $Z/T$ and every generic point $\xi$ of $Z_k$, $A=\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ is a DVR, the image of $\pi$ is a uniformizer, and for its fraction field $L$ the canonical extension $E\to L$ and pulled-back form $\omega_L$ give minimum $n_0$; the component opens of the list after base change represent all minimal $A$-models, also for every permitted shrinking of the list.
